consensus_summary: The consensus identifies the poor, meek, and needy primarily as the humble and faithful who recognize their spiritual poverty and depend wholly on God (the 'anawim'), often contrasted with the proud and self-sufficient, while also recognizing literal socioeconomic dimensions.
book_summary: The book identifies the poor, meek, and needy as those who are bowed and empty-handed before God, receptive to His grace in contrast to the self-sufficient.
consensus_core_identification: The humble who depend entirely on God rather than their own resources.
book_core_identification: Those bowed and empty-handed before God, able to receive what the self-sufficient refuse.
rationale: The book's definition perfectly matches the primary consensus definition of the 'anawim'—those who are spiritually humble, dependent upon God, and stripped of self-sufficiency, allowing them to receive the kingdom.
